text:
sasha: quick FYI — after last canary with hybrid fp8+4bit profiles we saw a spike in quality regressions for a subset of long-code prompts. Not huge, but noticeable. Repro steps and logs below. Need to decide fallback signaling for runtime and API-level tolerance policy. cc @jonah @maria

jonah: thanks. can you paste the minimal repro?

sasha: pasted:
```
POST /v1/generate
model: redwood-large-arch
input: long code block (~1200 tokens)
profile: hybrid-fp8-4b-hotpath
```

sasha: snippet from eval run:
```
metric: exact_match
baseline: 0.983
canary: 0.947
samples: 200
```

maria: that's bigger than our threshold (0.01 delta). Did runtime auto-fallback trigger?

sasha: no — runtime didn't because the profile passed per-batch loss gate. Looks like per-token drift accumulates.

devon: maybe we need a "cumulative-deviation" detector in runtime that monitors moving-window quality proxies (e.g., logprob drop). Fallback on exceed.

kevin: agree. also want API-level flag: response_quality_tolerance: {mode: soft|strict, delta: 0.01} 

jonah: proposed config snippet:
```yaml
quant_profiles:
  - name: hybrid-fp8-4b-hotpath
    fallback_policy:
      monitor: moving_logprob_avg
      window: 50
      threshold: -0.15 # drop from baseline
      action: fallback_to:int8
```

maria: +1. Also add a canary-rollout weight floor for X% to collect metric.

sasha: ops-bot posted canary events during run: :ops-bot:
ops-bot: canary 2024-09-15T12:08Z: hybrid-fp8-4b-hotpath rollout 20% -> metric delta alerted

kevin: edge case: fallback_to:int8 might increase latency by 30ms; need to surface downstream and let API choose degrade vs retry.

devon: propose making fallback action pluggable: fallback_to, degrade_with_notes, throttle, reject. Default fallback to similar-precision model.

jonah: Also need eval harness to test accumulation scenarios. Maria can we add a longitudinal prompt set that stresses long contexts?

maria: I can add ~120 prompts to the "long-code" family and run nightly. I'll also add a regression alert if avg EM drops > 0.005 over 24h.

sasha: cool. next steps: implement moving-window detector in runtime, add YAML config options to quant_profiles, surface latency cost in console. I'll open RFC PR.

kevin: please tag infra for budget impacts.

sasha: opened PR 3145. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/3145

jonah: will review this morning.

maria: will prepare regression set.

devon: i'll prototype detector.

kevin: thx :thumbsup: 

sasha: thanks all.
